description: Saskatoon's 2024 Civic Services Survey shows 84% resident satisfaction.
Top concerns are homelessness, crime, and public safety.
Council requested survey data for diverse communities and by ward.

chips.text: Approved
Councillor Dubois urged immediate action on customer service; staff suggested strategic planning.
Why customer service and public engagement satisfaction scores declined remains unclear.

segments.title: 2024 Civic Services Survey Presentation
description: Administration presented results of two surveys conducted in May and June.
84% of residents are satisfied with living in Saskatoon.
Top issues identified were homelessness and crime/public safety.
Residents want more service in affordable housing and road maintenance.

chips.text: Saskatoon residents expressed satisfaction with city life and services.
Homelessness and crime were cited as top issues by residents.
Next civic services surveys are planned for May and June.

segments.title: Questions on Inter-City Issue Comparisons
description: Mayor Block asked about comparing Saskatoon's issues to other cities.
Administration stated direct correlation is difficult without deeper analysis.
Many issues like homelessness are frequently cited by other cities.

chips.text: Direct correlation between homelessness and overall satisfaction in other cities is unclear.

segments.title: Survey Methodology and Diverse Community Representation
description: Councillor Timon questioned online panel's ability to reach all residents.
Administration explained random sampling from a professional online panel.
Increasing sample size for full representation would increase costs.

chips.text: Survey methodology may not fully represent low-income or diverse communities.
Increasing sample size for full demographic representation would increase survey costs.

segments.title: Council Direction for Survey Enhancement
description: Chair asked if administration needed council direction for broader demographic representation.
Administration stated council direction would be beneficial due to potential costs.
Councillor Timon confirmed desire for further investigation into this.

chips.text: Administration indicated council direction would be helpful for survey enhancements.

segments.title: Declining Customer Service and Public Engagement Metrics
description: Councillor Dubois noted declines in customer service and public engagement metrics.
Administration observed results are similar to pre-COVID 2018 levels.
City is interested in better understanding and improving customer experience.

chips.text: Councillor Dubois expressed concern over significant declines in customer service metrics.

segments.title: Administration's Response to Customer Service Concerns
description: Councillor Dubois pressed for immediate action on customer service declines.
Administration stated results are shared with departments for operational work.
Strategic planning process will incorporate these findings for future actions.
Follow-up questions can be included in the next annual survey.

chips.text: Administration will use survey results to inform operational work and future business plans.

segments.title: Data Collection Methods and Statistical Analysis
description: Councillor Pierce asked about data sources and methodology for the report.
Administration confirmed consistent use of 800 online panel respondents.
Explained statistical significance of homelessness/crime on quality of life.

chips.text: Full demographic and ward-based representation in the survey is challenging due to sample size.

segments.title: Ongoing Customer Service Monitoring Between Surveys
description: Councillor Jeffries asked about checks on customer service levels between annual surveys.
Question was about private sector-like follow-up surveys after interactions.
Administration will follow up with the Service Saskatoon team for information.

chips.text: Current methods for monitoring customer service between annual surveys are unclear.

segments.title: Chair's Questions on Survey Format and Administrative Response
description: Chair confirmed the online survey process is consistent with past methods.
Asked Mr. Jordanson about administrative response to declining categories.
Administration will dig in and bring ideas to strategic planning.

chips.text: Administration will investigate declining categories and bring ideas to strategic planning.

segments.title: Chair's Call for Administrative Action Plan
description: Chair requested an administrative response on plans to address declining categories.
Asked for action plans and appropriate KPIs for strategic planning.
Suggested future reports include trend analysis beyond year-to-year comparisons.

chips.text: Chair requested administration to present action plans and KPIs for strategic planning.

segments.title: Motion to Enhance Survey for Diverse Views and Ward Data
description: Councillor Timon moved for a report on enhancing the survey for diverse community views.
Councillor Pierce amended to include options for ward-by-ward responses.
The motion requests a report back before the next multi-year budget.

chips.text: Motion amended to include reporting on ward-by-ward responses.
Motion requests a report back on survey enhancement options.

segments.title: Mayor Block's Comments and Survey Motion Vote
description: Mayor Block appreciated discussion on diverse feedback and the co-motion.
Defended customer service staff, highlighting their hard work and empathy.
Noted declining public respect since COVID, asking how to change the culture.
Councillor Timon's amended motion carried unanimously.

chips.text: Motion to report on enhancing survey for diverse views and ward data carried unanimously.
The motion carried unanimously.
Mayor Block highlighted the challenge of declining public respect towards staff.

description: David Fineday advocated for Indigenous-led support for unhoused people.
City staff updated on $4.5 million for housing and navigation hub study.
Discussion covered service access and reasons for choosing to live rough.

chips.text: Received as information
Mayor Block expressed concern about the city's communication strategy for unhoused residents.
Roughly 36% of unhoused individuals choose to live rough, often on the east side.
Question raised about establishing a homeless shelter on the city's east side.
David Fineday, a hereditary chief, shared personal stories of friends lost to homelessness.

segments.title: David Fineday's appeal for homeless support
description: Speaker lost friends to homelessness, prompting action.
Challenges council to engage with unhoused people at night.
Advocates for funding Station 20 as a safe, home-like space.
Proposes a 24/7 First Nations smudge and prayer space.

chips.text: $1.2 million and $4.5 million mentioned for homeless initiatives.
Advocates for First Nations-led initiatives and culturally safe spaces for unhoused people.

segments.title: Mayor Block questions Fineday on effective support
description: Mayor Block acknowledges city's efforts in housing and support.
Asks Fineday about most effective ways to help unhoused people.
Inquires about gaps in existing smudging services.
Asks what makes Station 20's approach successful.

chips.text: Mayor Block asks about the importance of smudging for unhoused individuals.
Mayor Block notes the city is on the front lines but lacks all tools to solve crisis.

segments.title: Councillor Timo on collaboration and traditional ceremonies
description: Councillor Timo acknowledges city's funding for shelters.
Asks how existing wellness centers can collaborate with Station 20.
Inquires about reaching community partners for traditional ceremonies.
Fineday states he has tried to reach out to organizations without success.

chips.text: Councillor Timo asks how wellness centers can collaborate with Station 20
Councillor Timo asks about expanding traditional ceremonies like smudging.
David Fineday expresses frustration with organizations not collaborating or sharing funding.

segments.title: Councillor Pierce offers to connect with Fineday
description: Councillor Pierce expresses shared passion for helping people.
Asks Fineday if he can obtain his contact information.
Offers to join Fineday on a 2 AM tour to talk to unhoused people.
Fineday describes his Pleasant Hill tours to raise awareness.

chips.text: Councillor Pierce offers to connect with David Fineday and join his outreach efforts.
David Fineday describes his tours of Pleasant Hill to show the reality of homelessness.

segments.title: Administration updates on housing funding and hub feasibility
description: Administration confirms $4.5 million funding is for transitional and supportive housing.
Notes that converting funding to housing takes many months to years.
Feasibility study for a hub model is underway.
Hub model aims to centralize access to services for unhoused individuals.

chips.text: $4.5 million approved for transitional and supportive housing.
Feasibility study for a hub model is being conducted.
Administration is fast-tracking the process to get funding to partners.

segments.title: Discussion on communication for unhoused resources
description: Mayor Block asks how to ensure unhoused people are aware of resources.
Administration states connections happen through partners and mobile units.
Mayor Block questions if 911 is the best way for residents to help.
Staff confirm no single direct number for non-emergency support.

segments.title: Data on individuals choosing to live unhoused
description: Mayor Block asks about the percentage of people choosing to live rough.
SFD data indicates roughly 36% of reported cases choose to live rough.
Reasons include geographical comfort and feeling safer on the east side.
SFD emphasizes they are not the solution to homelessness.

chips.text: Roughly 36% of reported unhoused individuals choose to live rough, often on the east side.

segments.title: Library's role in supporting unhoused individuals
description: Councillor Parker asks about engaging the public library system for navigation tools.
Library plays a critical role in extreme weather strategies.
Library employs social workers and actively engages with partners.
They help connect individuals to services.

chips.text: Public library system provides critical support and navigation for unhoused individuals.
EMO coordinates partners, including the library, for extreme weather strategies.

segments.title: Service Saskatoon contact for non-emergency support
description: Councillor Timo asks for a direct phone number for non-emergency help.
Assistant Chief Ramer provides the Service Saskatoon number.
Information on emergency vs. non-emergency contacts will be shared.

chips.text: Service Saskatoon phone number 306-975-2476 provided for non-emergency support.
Information on emergency and non-emergency contacts will be shared with council.

segments.title: Mayor Block's concluding remarks and motion to receive
description: Mayor Block thanks Fineday and staff for the robust conversation.
Advocates for better communication strategy, noting current challenges.
Highlights council's focus on a new, community-wide approach to homelessness.
Moves to receive the information.

chips.text: Information received unanimously.
Mayor Block acknowledges David Fineday as a 60s Scoop survivor and values his input.
